profile.grounding_note: Simulated coaching profile grounded in real StudentLife pre-term surveys (PSS=24.0, PHQ-9=6.0, UCLA Loneliness=32.0, PHQ-9 item 9=0, Extraversion=1.75, Neuroticism=4.25, Conscientiousness=3.56); courses: COSC 065, COSC 027.
goals: Reduce high stress (PSS=24.0) during COSC 065 and COSC 027 labs with short restorative micro-breaks
Keep a consistent evening wind-down routine without feeling pressured into heavy workouts
Break lab assignments into small, concrete next steps when feeling overwhelmed

preferences.activity_style: Quiet indoor micro-breaks (stretching, deep breathing, warm tea)

constraints: High baseline perceived stress (PSS=24.0) and neuroticism (4.25) with low extraversion (1.75)
Studies frequently in quiet campus spaces and prefers low-friction resets

episodes.final_message: With 1 deadline today and another coming up over the next 3 days during midterms, it's completely understandable that homework is feeling overwhelming right now. Instead of tackling everything at once, pick just one priority task and work on a small, well-defined step for 25 minutes, then take a quiet break to reset with some warm tea or stretching.

simulated_feedback.feedback_text: Please don't suggest running, jogging, or going to the gym—I hate working out when I have CS deadlines. I prefer quiet indoor stretching, deep breathing, or making a cup of tea.

episodes.final_message: With a deadline due today and midterm stress running high, you've been working hard. Before diving back into your next study block, take a quick 5-minute break to step away from your screen, stretch, and make a warm cup of tea.

simulated_feedback.feedback_text: That quiet indoor break idea was much better. Also note that I study late at Baker-Berry Library, so keep suggestions library-compatible and super brief (under 35 words).
